# JNumberTools

> Zero-dependency Java 21+ library for deterministic combinatorics, arbitrary-precision (`BigInteger`) ranking/unranking, lexicographical sampling, and Cartesian products with compiled constraints.

JNumberTools provides lazy iterator/stream generators and mathematical utilities.

## Coordinates & runtime

- Maven: `io.github.deepeshpatel:jnumbertools:4.2.0`
- Java: 21+
- Runtime dependencies: none
- License: Apache-2.0

## Public API packages

- `io.github.deepeshpatel.jnumbertools.entrypoint`: static entry points `Permutation`, `Combination`, `Subset`, `Derangement`, `Product`, `Rank`, and `Unrank`.
- `io.github.deepeshpatel.jnumbertools.builders`: builder implementations returned by the entry points.
- `io.github.deepeshpatel.jnumbertools.datastructure`: `Calculator` and supporting data structures.
- `io.github.deepeshpatel.jnumbertools.numbersystem`: Factoradic, Permutadic and Combinadic representations; Derangadic is in `numbersystem.derangadic`.

Do not use the removed `JNumberTools` facade or assume that all builders expose the same terminal operations.

## Capability map

| Requirement | Entry point | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Unique, k-, repetitive or multiset permutations | `Permutation` | `unique(...)`, `nPk(...)`, `repetitive(...)`, `multiset(...)` |
| Unique, repetitive or multiset combinations | `Combination` | `unique(...)`, `repetitive(...)`, `multiset(...)` |
| Power set or subsets within a size range | `Subset` | `Subset.of(...).all()` or `.inRange(from,to)` |
| Derangements | `Derangement` | `Derangement.of(...)` |
| Simple Cartesian product | `Product.simple(List<?>...)` | One list per dimension |
| Constrained Cartesian product | `Product.constrained()` | Start with `ofDistinct`, `ofMultiSelect` or `ofInRange`; extend with matching builder methods |
| Pairwise conditional product | `Product.conditional(List<?>...)` | Compiled pairwise `.when(...).then(...)` rules |
| Joint lambda predicates | `Product.conditional(...).withLambda(...)` | Typed overloads for 1–5 dimensions; array form for arbitrary dimensions |
| Rank a permutation or derangement | `Rank.permutation()` | `unique`, `k`, `repetitive`, `multiset`, `derangement` |
| Rank a combination | `Rank.combination()` | `unique`, `repetitive`, `multiset` |
| Unrank a permutation or derangement | `Unrank.permutation()` | `unique`, `uniqueMinimumSize`, `k`, `repetitive`, `multiset`, `derangement` |
| Unrank a combination | `Unrank.combination()` | `unique`, `repetitive`, `multiset` |
| Combinatorial arithmetic | `new Calculator()` | BigInteger factorials, binomials, permutations, subfactorials and related functions |
| Number-system conversions | `Factoradic.of`, `Permutadic.of`, `Combinadic.of`, `new Derangadic(...)` | Use the representation classes directly |

## Examples

```java
import io.github.deepeshpatel.jnumbertools.entrypoint.*;
import io.github.deepeshpatel.jnumbertools.datastructure.Calculator;
import io.github.deepeshpatel.jnumbertools.numbersystem.*;
import io.github.deepeshpatel.jnumbertools.numbersystem.derangadic.Derangadic;
import java.math.BigInteger;
import java.util.List;

var all = Permutation.unique("A", "B", "C").lexOrder();
var chosen = Combination.unique(2, "A", "B", "C").sample(2, new java.util.Random());
var product = Product.simple(List.of("Linux", "Windows"), List.of("Firefox", "Safari"));

BigInteger rank = Rank.permutation().unique(2, 0, 1);
int[] decoded = Unrank.permutation().unique(rank, 3);

Calculator calculator = new Calculator();
Factoradic f = Factoradic.of(859);
Permutadic p = Permutadic.of(BigInteger.valueOf(100), 3);
Combinadic c = Combinadic.of(BigInteger.valueOf(35), 3, calculator);
Derangadic d = new Derangadic(4, BigInteger.valueOf(2), calculator);
```

## Semantic contracts

- Ranks are zero-based and represented by `BigInteger`.
- `count()` returns `BigInteger`.
- `lexOrder()` guarantees lexicographical order.
- `lexOrderMth(m,start)` and `byRanks(...)` are available only on builder types that document them.
- `choice(n, random)` samples with replacement; `sample(n, random)` samples without replacement.
- Generators are lazy and re-iterable. Use `.stream()` to consume them as streams.
- The Compiled Conditional Product supports pairwise rules and rank-based operations. Lambda rules compile bounded joint predicates into constraints; do not assume the Lambda Engine has the same traversal operations as every other product builder.
- The Calculator may be shared across entry points that accept it, allowing combinatorial caches to be reused.
